objects.name: Voyager 1
objects.facts: The most distant human-made object. It crossed the heliopause into interstellar space in August 2012.

objects.name: Voyager 2
objects.facts: The only spacecraft to have visited Uranus and Neptune. It entered interstellar space in November 2018.

objects.name: New Horizons
objects.facts: Flew past Pluto on 14 July 2015 and the Kuiper Belt object Arrokoth on 1 January 2019.

objects.name: Parker Solar Probe
objects.facts: Repeated Venus flybys shrink its orbit around the Sun. In December 2024 it passed about 6.1 million km from the solar surface at about 192 km/s.

objects.name: 1P/Halley
objects.facts: Returns roughly every 76 years. Last at perihelion on 9 February 1986, next expected in July 2061.

objects.name: 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko
objects.facts: Target of ESA's Rosetta mission, which landed the Philae probe on it in November 2014. Perihelion was on 13 August 2015.

objects.name: C/1995 O1 (Hale-Bopp)
objects.facts: Reached perihelion on 1 April 1997 and was visible to the naked eye for about 18 months. Its orbit takes more than two thousand years.

objects.name: 1 Ceres
objects.facts: The largest object in the asteroid belt and the only dwarf planet in the inner solar system. The Dawn spacecraft orbited it from 2015.

objects.name: 4 Vesta
objects.facts: One of the largest and most massive asteroids. The Dawn spacecraft orbited it from 2011 to 2012.

objects.name: 433 Eros
objects.facts: A near-Earth asteroid about 34 km long. NEAR Shoemaker orbited it and landed on it on 12 February 2001.

objects.name: 101955 Bennu
objects.facts: About 490 m across. OSIRIS-REx collected a sample in 2020 and returned it to Earth in September 2023.

objects.name: 99942 Apophis
objects.facts: About 340 m across. On 13 April 2029 it will pass about 32,000 km above Earth, inside the orbit of geostationary satellites.
